Theme

School & learning · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

Greek noun

the language

also the Greek language, Ancient Greek, in Greek, know Greek, speak Greek, write Greek

classical

Cic. Fin. 1.10 (Lewis & Short)

lingua Graeca

the Greek language

For a Roman it was the other language: utraque lingua, both languages, is Greek and Latin (see language).

Other words

  • sermō Graecus — Greek speech, the Greek language

    also used · classical · Quint. 1.1.12: ā sermōne Graecō puerum incipere mālō

  • Graecē — in Greek

    adverb · also used · classical · Plaut. Merc. 9: Graecē haec vocātur Emporos; Cic. Tusc. 1.15: Graecē loquī

    See speak, a language.

  • litterae Graecae — Greek letters: the language and its literature as a study

    also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 26: litterās Graecās senex didicī; Quint. 12.11.23

    To learn Greek is litterās Graecās discere: Cato learned it as an old man (Cic. Sen. 26; Quint. 12.11.23).

Examples

  • Graecē haec vocātur Emporos Philēmōnis, eadem Latīnē Mercātor Maccī Titī

    In Greek this play is called Philemon’s Emporos; in Latin it is the Mercator of Titus MacciusPlaut. Merc. 9–10

  • Graeca leguntur in omnibus ferē gentibus, Latīna suīs fīnibus exiguīs sānē continentur

    Greek is read among almost every people, while Latin is kept within its own borders, and narrow onesCic. Arch. 23

  • et ego fēcī quī litterās Graecās senex didicī

    and so did I, who learned Greek as an old manCic. Sen. 26

  • Graecē scīre (loquī, scrībere)

    to know (speak, write) GreekTraupman 324

See also Latin, language, speak, translate.
